name: Cometly
description: Marketing attribution and analytics for B2B SaaS — sends accurate attribution data back to ad platforms; AI chat over ads data. Founded Oct  mid-2020, US. High ACV (291 subs → ~$206k MRR).

mentions.evidence: ~$206,311 MRR, 291 active subscriptions, ~$253,748 L30, ~$9,929,042 all-time, ~90% L30 profit margin. Last sync Oct 3, 2026 ~04:13 Warsaw (02:13 UTC).
mentions.indieAngle: Narrow attribution for one channel stack (Meta+Stripe, or LinkedIn+HubSpot) and charge for "which ad paid the invoice." High ACV, small logo count.

whyItPrints: Ads attribution plumbing. SaaS teams pay to know which campaigns closed revenue; once pixels and CRM sync live, churn is painful. Analytics infra with fat seats, not consumer virality.
whyThisMatters:
B2B teams use Cometly to see which ads turned into revenue. Marketing, sales, and product data go into one view: a pixel, server-side tracking, multi-touch attribution, and events. Dashboards show the path an account took. You can ask an agent about the numbers.

Attribution syncs into the CRM, a warehouse, and back to the ad accounts. Meta, Google, and LinkedIn are the networks. Stripe is how a paid subscription gets tied to the click. They say more than 70 tools connect. An agency can keep one workspace per client. There's an ads manager and audiences if you want to spend against what closed. An MCP hook is part of the sync.

Sales teams use it to see which ads booked demos and closed. Product-led teams follow a signup until it becomes a paying customer. Agency partners can earn a commission on clients they refer. The company is in the US and started in mid-2020. The point is a closed deal tied back to the ad that started it.
